paragraphs: Lexipol sells policy manuals, training, wellness resources, performance reporting, and grant support to public safety agencies, delivered through one system. Its buyers are the people running those agencies, from fire and police chiefs to risk managers, dispatch supervisors, and city administrators. An agency can begin with a single product, such as Policy or Wellness, and add others as it goes.

The policy product is the core: state-specific manuals researched and written by policy and legal professionals, then kept current as laws and standards change. Personnel acknowledge each policy electronically, which creates an audit trail for accreditation, audits, or legal reviews. Daily Training Bulletins turn those policies into practice through short scenario-based lessons. The LexOne platform ties training assignments to policy, warns leaders when licenses or credentials are about to expire, and tracks the data agencies need for reporting. Online courses carry accreditation from organizations such as IADLEST, POST, and CAPCE.

Lexipol was created in 2003 by two attorneys who were also former law enforcement officers. Co-founder Gordon Graham still records a weekly two-minute video tip for public safety and local government personnel. The company says its wellness product alone supports more than 1,000 agencies across the U.S. and Canada. Among the chiefs quoted on the site, Edward Delmore of the Gulf Shores (AL) Police Department compares a subscription to having another full-time administrator assigned to policy.
